hints: For each quantity type, decide whether its description needs only size or also a specified direction.
walkthrough: A scalar quantity is fully described by its magnitude, so no direction is needed.
A vector quantity needs both a magnitude and a direction to be fully specified.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a scalar quantity has magnitude only.
States that a vector quantity has magnitude and direction.

hints: For each listed quantity, ask whether a direction is required as well as its size.
walkthrough: A scalar has magnitude only, whereas a vector has both magnitude and direction.
Power is a rate of energy transfer and temperature gives thermal state, so neither needs a direction: both are scalars.
Momentum depends on velocity and therefore has a direction, so it is a vector.

ai_rubric.observable: Classifies power and temperature as scalars and momentum as a vector; award one mark for two correct classifications and two marks for all three.

hints: Treat the aircraft and wind velocities as vectors; the resultant joins the start of the first vector to the final endpoint after vector addition.
walkthrough: The aircraft velocity is westward, while the wind velocity has a westward component and a northward component.
Adding the two vectors therefore gives a resultant that is mainly westward but tilted north of west.
Draw an arrow in that direction on Fig. 1.2 and label it R; its direction is about 13° north of west.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws and labels R in a direction between 5° and 20° north of west.

hints: Resolve the wind velocity into components parallel and perpendicular to the aircraft's westward velocity.
Add the westward components, retain the northward component, then use Pythagoras for the resultant magnitude.
walkthrough: The wind has a westward component 28 cos 65° = 11.8 m s⁻¹ and a northward component 28 sin 65° = 25.4 m s⁻¹.
The resultant components are therefore 95 + 11.8 = 106.8 m s⁻¹ west and 25.4 m s⁻¹ north.
To appropriate precision, the magnitude of the resultant velocity is 110 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses a valid component or cosine-rule relation for the resultant speed, or draws a correctly scaled velocity triangle.
Obtains a resultant speed of 110 m s⁻¹, accepting a correctly read scale-diagram value from 108 to 112 m s⁻¹.
